industry.why: Overweight, carried. Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-11-06 against 2026-09-04, not week on week: B now, A prior at the industry, with Downstream distribution A, Upstream A, Services D and Metals and mining F inside it. No Brent level reached the pack, so the condition (Brent under $85) is untested, and the undated headline that oil is dipping on peace hopes is noted, not acted on. Component 1 regime, 6-Nov-26 (risk-off beneath an index at its high, now present in Europe's own prices: the STOXX Europe 600 0.9% from its 52-week high with the share of stocks above the 100, 150 and 200-day averages at or below the tenth percentile of near-high days since 2006, defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows, breadth recovering for a second week; the causes, inflation, rates, yields, credit and the consumer, unread this week because the strategist and newsletter files did not reach the pack, so the credit-and-cost-of-debt read of 30-Oct-26 with the US ten-year above 5% is held one week stale; sources present 2026-W45, headline-only): energy is still the hedge inside a European book against the shock that hurts everything else, and the hedge has not been needed for two weeks. Eight of the top 40 on the starting score are energy names, from 15 last week, as Neste and Galp left the Pool. Counter-case: the tilt scorecard's negative spreads are consistent with the Overweight having been paid already, and a ceasefire would take the premium out. To C if Brent is read under $85 or the industry's relative strength falls to C.

Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-30 against 2026-08-28, not week on week: A now, A prior, agrees. Eighteen Pool names, the largest sector in the Pool, with 15 energy names in the top 40 of the starting score, which is why the sector cap on the Lists (component 5, amendment 6) stays. Counter-case: producers move with crude and crude eased late in the week. Back to C if Brent falls under $85.

memo.verdict: Bearish; park. The record calls MOL Hungarian Oil & Gas a cyclical peak dressed as a change case and recommends standing aside at HUF 5,000 (2026-10-08). Conviction: high on the park, medium on the direction of earnings (the margin could hold longer than we think), high on the valuation (the multiple is at the top of its range on any reading). The park is argued on the 'Modal return' (F) and the valuation (F), not on a gate: the park rule's gates do not bite (management C, business quality C, predictability C, trackability B). What would bring the case back: a price near HUF 2,500 on our path; a price near HUF 3,500 with the multiple proved to hold; or the earnings path proved higher by two reported quarters of Brent-based complex refining margins above USD 15 per barrel (Q4 2026 and Q1 2027) with FY2027 consensus not cut, which would move the thesis to C and the return to B on the bull branch. The record states it is not betting but standing aside from a bet the market is making, that a conflict-driven refining windfall is durable and that a Hungarian landlocked refiner under a 95 percent windfall tax deserves Shell's multiple, and would take the other side at about HUF 2,500.
case: - The change is external and already reversing. The Q2 2026 earnings were made by a conflict-driven spike in European refining and petrochemical margins (USD 20.8 per barrel; EUR 548 per tonne) that the sell-side attributes to temporary supply bottlenecks in middle distillates; the petrochemical half reversed to EUR 119 per tonne inside a month, and management expects refining margins to contract over eighteen months. The 'Demand Inflection' test is not met: CEE fuel demand grew 1 percent in Q2 2026 and 2 percent in H1 2026; the thing that moved was a supply-side spread without two years' visibility.

- The other external forces are headwinds that are intensifying: political and regulatory F (the state taking more, not less, with a 7 percent deficit behind it); the company's own cycle at a peak D (consensus EBITDA minus 12.6 percent in FY2027); crude supply D (Druzhba shut for nearly three months; Adria at three to four times fair fees and about 80 percent of needs); competition D (Orlen's 3,500-station target and seaborne Saudi crude under long-term contract; structural petrochemical imports). Macro nets to a mild headwind (the forint's 13 percent appreciation shrinks dollar earnings in HUF).

- The internal change is real, modest and slow, and it is not what moved the earnings. Two of twelve internal forces are strong (new geographies B: Aphrodite, Azerbaijan, Libya, NIS; shareholder returns B: the 9.1 percent dividend rise), six moderate, four absent or negative (no chief-executive change D; no guidance rise D; no perimeter reduction D; price rises F under caps). Project HIVE doubled turnover to 13 percent. The screen's rule is not met.
counter_case: - At its strongest (Building Block 1): European middle-distillate markets have tightened structurally, not cyclically. Refinery closures across Europe, sanctions on Russian products, Hormuz risk and a diesel-heavy Central European demand base mean cracks settle well above the old normal, say USD 12 to 15 per barrel, for years; the sell-side's framing is a global "Golden Age" of refining (5-Aug-26) and weighted cracks were near USD 45 per barrel in July 2026. MOL is the purest listed expression: 48 percent of production is diesel, its plants are in the top European net cash margin quartile, and from September 2026 the Danube refinery runs at full capacity after a year at half, so FY2027 volumes rise even as margins ease. Tomorrow Downstream adds USD 500 million a year by 2027. The balance sheet is at 0.49x with USD 5.0 billion of liquidity, the dividend yields 6 percent and is rising, the Croatian overhang on the Chairman-CEO is gone, the foundation dissolution returns 5.2 percent of shares to treasury, Aphrodite is a long-dated gas option, NIS a consolidation option, the HUF 126 billion carbon-tax claim is upside. On that reading the historical 5 to 6x was a discount for problems being solved, consensus FY2027 EPS of HUF 625 is too low, the sell-side's bull case is HUF 6,307, and a stock at 7.9x one-year-forward earnings with a 6 percent yield is not expensive.

- Conceded: H2 2026 will probably be strong and FY2026 consensus will probably rise (July cracks, the Danube restart, the insurance receipt); the dividend is real and its base is safe; the balance sheet is clean; the legal overhang is resolved; the mix drifts toward retail; a sustained margin above USD 15 per barrel is possible at about 30 percent, and on that branch the stock is a B over eighteen months.
triggers: - Invalidate: Brent-based complex refining margins above USD 15 per barrel sustained through Q4 2026 and Q1 2027 with FY2027 consensus not cut; this moves the thesis to C and the return to B on the bull branch. Alarm: a reported quarter below USD 10 per barrel confirms the case.

- Invalidate: a legislated rollback of the Brent-Urals tax and the caps by Q1 2027. Alarm: a further decree. The 95 percent tax expires end-2026; the HUF 126 billion CO2 claim is a possible rollback signal.

- Invalidate: the multiple falling to 6.5x with earnings holding above HUF 600, from which the case would clear the bar from a lower entry. Alarm: the 24-month-forward P/E above 10x (the market pricing a structural re-rating). What would change our mind on the multiple: it holding above 8x through a quarter in which FY2027 consensus is cut 10 percent.

- Re-entry prices: about HUF 2,500 on our path (HUF 2,538 at eighteen months; HUF 2,331 at three years); about HUF 3,500 (HUF 3,496) if the multiple is proved to hold at 9.2x. TSR/Valuation re-bases the three fixed lines nightly; the F stands until the price is near HUF 2,500 or the earnings path is proved higher.

- Supply: a second multi-month Druzhba outage invalidates the logistics assumption; a Druzhba interruption of weeks or a JANAF ultimatum alarms; a JANAF settlement at a fair tariff would move the view up. The Adria capacity tests run to January 2027; the DG Competition complaint is pending; USD 500 million of debottlenecking to process non-Russian crude is due by end-2026.

- Dividend and balance sheet: net debt to EBITDA above 1.0x after the Aphrodite payment (early 2027), or a cut to the HUF 120 special in April 2027, changes the cash-return assumption; consensus covers the FY2027 dividend twice on free cash flow of HUF 506,293 million.
